desc:
Given an integer array nums, a window length k and an integer threshold, count the contiguous blocks of exactly k elements whose average is at least threshold.

nums = [2, 2, 2, 2, 5, 5, 5, 8], k = 3, threshold = 4
windows: [2,2,2] [2,2,2] [2,2,5] [2,5,5] [5,5,5] [5,5,8]
averages: 2, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
result = 3
hints: Computing every window's sum from scratch costs O(n * k).
Consecutive windows share k - 1 elements, so one sum can be updated into the next in O(1).
Avoid fractions: a window's average is at least threshold exactly when its sum is at least k * threshold.
editorial: Keep the sum of the current window. Moving the window one step right adds the new element and removes the one that left, so each window costs O(1).

Compare the sum against k * threshold instead of dividing, which keeps everything in exact integer arithmetic (no rounding questions with negative numbers). Count the windows that pass. Time O(n), extra space O(1).
